LFM3-1.7Bが本当にコーディング能力が高いのかテストした

LFM3-1.7B (thinking on, card-recommended sampling) works as a Claude Code backend for small, well-specified tasks. It fixed multi-file bugs, implemented a topological sort, extended a CLI, and answered a repo-exploration question, usually in 15–60 s per easy task and 2.5–6 min per hard task.

LFM3-Omni-2B (non-reasoning) does not: it called non-existent tools, overwrote test files with weaker ones, and looped on identical failed calls.

Qwen3.5-4B, in this particular setup, did worse than the smaller LFM3-1.7B — mostly because of runaway generations (a single reply running to the 20,000-token cap, ~8–10 min each) and, in 3 of 5 hard tasks (h2–h4), reporting success that the files on disk did not support (h2 and h4: no code written at all). See caveats: this is one trial per task and says little about Qwen's quality in other harnesses.
